item.research_question: How do the microstructure and mechanical properties of novel high-strength, low-activation Wx(TaVZr)100−x refractory high entropy alloys (RHEAs) change with varying W content?
item.processing_route: vacuum arc melting under a Ti-gettered, high-purity argon atmosphere, with 12 remelting cycles
item.test_conditions: room temperature (RT) compression tests at an initial strain rate of 5 × 10−4 s−1
key_findings: The RHEAs possess a disordered BCC phase, ordered Laves phase, and Zr-rich HCP phase
The yield strength of the RHEAs increases with increasing W content, reaching a maximum value of 1985 MPa in the W20 RHEA
The hardness value also increases with increasing W content
The microstructure of the RHEAs changes significantly with increasing W content, from a slender dendrite shape to a coarser dendrite shape
The distribution of dendrites becomes denser with increasing W content
Microcracks initially form in interdendritic regions during compression, and molten droplets also form in interdendritic regions on the fracture surface

records.text: Paper card. Question: How do the microstructure and mechanical properties of novel high-strength, low-activation Wx(TaVZr)100−x refractory high entropy alloys (RHEAs) change with varying W content?. System: Wx(TaVZr)100−x (x = 5, 10, 15, 20, 25) refractory high entropy alloys. Processing: vacuum arc melting under a Ti-gettered, high-purity argon atmosphere, with 12 remelting cycles. Test conditions: room temperature (RT) compression tests at an initial strain rate of 5 × 10−4 s−1. Findings: The RHEAs possess a disordered BCC phase, ordered Laves phase, and Zr-rich HCP phase; The yield strength of the RHEAs increases with increasing W content, reaching a maximum value of 1985 MPa in the W20 RHEA; The hardness value also increases with increasing W content; The microstructure of the RHEAs changes significantly with increasing W content, from a slender dendrite shape to a coarser dendrite shape; The distribution of dendrites becomes denser with increasing W content; Microcracks initially form in interdendritic regions during compression, and molten droplets also form in interdendritic regions on the fracture surface; The fracture mode of the RHEAs changes from initial intergranular fractures to a mixed fracture mode featuring the coexistence of both intergranular and transgranular fractures with increasing applied load. Mechanism: The improvement in strength and hardness is mainly due to solid solution strengthening and the increase in dendritic regions. Quote: "The RHEAs demonstrate high strength and hardness, with these properties being higher than in most reported tungsten-containing RHEAs"
